prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to outbound load control handoff; airline loading excluded. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (congestion thresholds, overload response, recovery authorization, isolated-bag notices, priority for earlier flights, may defer bags; releases to make-up only within flight processing window; coordinates build priority with airline ground ops). Security Duty Manager (alarm decisions; resolves security release holds before departure build). Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (security holds; Custody Seal Log). Maintenance Technician (isolates failures, confirms route safe, reports lane restrictions). Airline Ramp Coordinator (sends Carousel Release Slip to Carousel 7; confirms staffing/equipment/loading sequence before accepting build). Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk; stages bags keeping flight association); Bag Tag Printer (Calibration Witness Tag; replacement tags only after authorized confirmation); Transfer Bag Feeder (Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station; meters without bypassing checks); Induction Tray Conveyor (priority admission, scan confirmation, spacing, meters to avoid make-up accumulation). Interlocks stop feed on jam/open door/downstream not ready. Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (tag-flight link; sort plan validation; cutoff profiles; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; alternate route only if screening/timing valid; diverts to Secondary Inspection Chute; records screening disposition/release state per flight). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive; capacity; Recovery Route Card; assigns make-up lanes). Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight identity/timing, dispatch targets; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory). Screening: North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel, and South Gate Scanner (outcomes, ID verification; Manual Rescan Receipt); Image Resolution Desk; Secondary Inspection Chute (holds until disposition); Bag Reconciliation Station (Bag Match Query). Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (routes by destination/priority/status; Chute Occupancy Note). Make-up: East/West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (order/position; slip only after checks); Outbound Load Control Desk (reconciles build vs permitted load). Requirements: hold bad-data bags; valid record/route/equipment for induction; incomplete exams never cleared; routing withheld pending image/security disposition; unscreened held; cutoffs include allowances; missed-cutoff held; manual resolution when

New part:
S156: Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
S157: The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
S158: The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
S159: Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
S160: When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
S161: The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
S162: Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
S163: Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
S164: Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
S165: A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
S166: Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
S167: Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
S168: North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
S169: Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
S170: Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
S171: Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
S172: After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
S173: Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
S174: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
S175: Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
S176: Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
S177: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
